original_card.question: Does the reported word-census parity-pruning error invalidate a specific exclusion we still rely on, and what bounded repair is justified?
methods: Independently reconstruct the tiny counterexample and trace one affected exclusion to its exact pruning code.
Compare corrected and unpruned enumeration on a small exhaustive domain, then audit the changed pruning implication.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Pin the old and proposed corrected engines, distinguish a disproved pruning rule from a disproved final bound, and state exactly which downstream exclusions need revalidation. #2973 is an author-checked source archive; neither its new f(7) claim nor all old conclusions are automatically accepted or rejected.

first_step.inspect: Resolve the current selected review, separate complex/ordinary BIT/admitted BIT/outer budgets, and compare the card against live handoffs before starting. Historical ceilings require exact source/model equivalence.
first_step.scope: Source-binding orientation only; not a scientific replay or all-size proof. Materialize selected inputs if this checkout is sparse.

original_card.first_experiment: Reconstruct the eight prefix states of 01021323 and compare bit-0 versus Hamming-weight parity budgets independently. Trace the reported false prune to one pinned predecessor (#2542, #2634 or #2691), then test a small exhaustive domain. Stop after a source-impact handoff or corrected-prune proof; a full seven-label replay needs a separate resource budget and a named research decision it can change.
original_card.bottleneck_link: An unsound exclusion can wrongly close a mechanism; correcting its dependency boundary is more useful than extending the same census.
allowed_variations: One predecessor pruning rule, one independently exhaustive small domain, or one downstream dependency audit.
scope_change_triggers: Launching a larger census before validating the prune and explaining which active decision it changes.
Treating a small-domain counterexample to the old rule as a counterexample to every reported seven-label bound.

actual_scope: Exact restriction-kernel evaluation of the complete PR1325 P112 plane-compatibility census, preserving its scientific receipt.
scope_change_reason: The donation requires original work rather than predecessor validation. This changes the audit card to an implementation-preservation proof and a new exact evaluation algorithm for the unchanged finite census.
bottleneck_link: Makes exact decoder screening cheaper without weakening finite coverage; supplies no physical COPY word or better exponent.
stop_rule: Ship the first verified complete-command improvement; do not extend the algorithm.
evidence: PROOF.md; full certificate and ordered stream comparison; exhaustive small-subspace conformance; alternating complete CLI benchmark.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Can the same restriction-kernel evaluator accelerate an explicitly different decoder census?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Larger source spaces make literal partner-vector scans expensive.
open_questions.first_step: Profile one complete command and expose its precise binary subspace restriction.
